sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Northern Adelbert Range languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-31. Canberra: ANU. (Bilakura = F18.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Introduction sec. 7 (pp. viii-ix): transcription 'semi-phonemic; i.e. apparently non-contrastive phonetic details are omitted'; Bilakura fluctuations w~g, g~l, s~ts listed. The words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur in the volume; F18 Bilakura forms (e.g. p. 17 = PDF p. 33: nose masilu, tongue kabisa) carry no stress marks.

sources.note: Lists only Pick 2020 (subclassification, pp. 188-194, 397-398) and Campbell et al. 2022 (ELCat endangerment); 0 descriptive references.

sources.citation: Pick, Andrew. 2020. A reconstruction of Proto-Northern Adelbert phonology and lexicon. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. 486 pp. ScholarSpace 10125/73354.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 1.5.1 'Stress' (pp. 31-32) covers only Mauwake, Pamosu and Usan and says 'the available data on stress in most languages are minimal or nonexistent'. Sec. 4.2 'Karian' (pp. 144-150: Boia/Barto varieties, phoneme tables 4.2.1a-b, morphophonology, verb morphology, based on Pick's 2017/2019 fieldwork with Anton Ake) and sec. 10.4 'Sound changes in Karian' (p. 425 ff.) contain no mention of stress or accent.
